ball_params — DRIVE ball op

• Data kinds: none → table (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.ball_params(radius: 'float' = 0.02, mass: 'float' = 0.0027, cd=0.4, cl=None, rho: 'float' = 1.2, g: 'float' = 9.81, shell: 'bool' = True, spin_decay: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import ballistics; ballistics.ball_params(radius: 'float' = 0.02, mass: 'float' = 0.0027, cd=0.4, cl=None, rho: 'float' = 1.2, g: 'float' = 9.81, shell: 'bool' = True, spin_decay: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("ball_params"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Ball table. The default is a table tennis ball (ITTF: diameter 40 mm, 2.7 g, thin shell).

cd = drag coefficient (a number, or "sphere" for the Re-dependent empirical formula drag_coefficient_sphere), cl = lift (Magnus) coefficient (None for the spin-ratio model of magnus_lift_coefficient, a number for a constant), rho = air density [kg/m³], spin_decay = spin decay rate [1/s] (dω/dt = −spin_decay·ω. 0 means no decay. A quantity to be identified from measurements).
